description: Fresh fictional native Step2 on/off fixtures. Authored and labeled before embeddings or retrieval outcomes. Labels are for scoring only and must never be passed into ranking. Supporting facts occupy distinct scenes/events unless copies are the intentional stress.

cases.query: Which two field-device constraints justified Cedar choosing SQLite?

memories.text: Cedar selected SQLite for the field-device journal.
Cedar needed writes to continue without Wi-Fi; this was one reason for choosing SQLite.
Cedar required committed journal entries to survive abrupt power loss; this drove the SQLite choice.
The Cedar SQLite test retained every committed journal entry after power cuts.
Cedar database-selection notes use the heading Field-device constraints.
The Cedar field-device case is green.
Birch chose PostgreSQL because its fleet has permanent network links.
Cedar keeps map thumbnails in a disposable cache.
The Cedar benchmark ran on a desktop connected to office Wi-Fi.

cases.evidence_notes: Both stated constraints are needed; a database name or heading alone does not answer why.

cases.query: What did Lumen release, and which observed check justified the release?

memories.text: Release Lumen with the resumable-upload path enabled.
Lumen resumed all 40 interrupted uploads without duplicate chunks; this check cleared the release.
The Lumen upload path persisted its chunk cursor before retrying.
Before testing, Lumen planned to validate resumable uploads.
Lumen release validation is the title of the checklist.
A draft announcement described Lumen as ready before validation completed.
The Lumen upload button uses a circular icon.
Nova released its batch-export path after a load test.
Lumen documentation includes an upload troubleshooting page.

cases.evidence_notes: An intention or announcement draft is not the observed release check.

cases.query: Which recurring Meridian failure motivated the checkpoint rule, and what two incidents support that pattern?

memories.text: Meridian must checkpoint before acknowledging work because restarts repeatedly lost uncheckpointed acknowledgements.
On September 10, Meridian acknowledged job A before checkpointing; a restart lost job A.
On September 12, Meridian acknowledged job B before checkpointing; another restart lost job B.
A Meridian restart test preserved acknowledged jobs after the checkpoint rule was added.
The Meridian retrospective has a section named Recurring checkpoint failures.
Meridian retried one timed-out metrics request.
Meridian log timestamps use UTC.
Aurora lost a job because its queue quota was exceeded.
Meridian README examples show the checkpoint API.

cases.evidence_notes: One incident does not establish the requested recurrence; all three claims remain separate.

cases.query: What was the order of Orion’s migration milestones: trial, approval, and production cutover?

memories.text: Orion completed the SQLite migration trial on September 4.
Orion approved the migration on September 8 after reviewing the trial.
Orion completed production cutover on September 14.
Orion’s retrospective links the trial, approval, and production-cutover notes.
On September 1, Orion proposed a production cutover for September 11; that date was not the actual cutover.
The Orion migration checklist lists trial, approval, and cutover as headings.
The Orion status page displays a new logo.
Vega completed its production cutover on September 6.
The Orion maintenance window permits work from 02:00 to 03:00 UTC.

cases.evidence_notes: Use observed milestone dates, not the abandoned proposal date.

cases.query: How did Maple’s authentication decision change, and what explicitly caused the correction?

memories.text: Maple’s initial decision was to keep local password login.
Correction: remove local password login from Maple and use company SSO.
Maple changed to company SSO because the signed enterprise contract required centralized account revocation.
Maple’s SSO test revoked a terminated account within one minute.
The Maple login screen uses a blue button.
An early Maple draft described password reset emails.
Elm retains local passwords because it serves independent accounts.
Maple authentication decision change is a heading in the release notes.
Maple exports daily authentication metrics.

cases.evidence_notes: The correction itself states the old-to-new authentication change; its explicit contract reason is also required. The earlier decision is useful context but not necessary.

cases.query: For Atlas production, what are the TLS and debug-log settings?

memories.text: Enable TLS for Atlas production traffic.
Disable debug logs for Atlas production traffic.
Atlas production accepted TLS connections and rejected plaintext HTTP.
Atlas production emitted no debug-level log messages during the release check.
Enable debug logs in the isolated Atlas lab environment.
Atlas production settings documentation contains TLS and debug-log sections.
Atlas production listens on port 8443.
Atlas backups run every night.
Comet production keeps debug logging enabled during its pilot.

cases.evidence_notes: Enable TLS and disable debug logs are compatible settings, not a change of view.

Harbor chose SQLite because committed surveys must survive an unexpected tablet restart.
Harbor uses SQLite on survey tablets.
Harbor uses SQLite on survey tablets.
Harbor uses SQLite on survey tablets.
Harbor uses SQLite on survey tablets.
Harbor uses SQLite on survey tablets.

Harbor survey tablets use waterproof cases.

The Kepler-West test submitted batches containing 64 records.

Solace chose exponential backoff on September 8 because immediate retries synchronized and overloaded the gateway.
Solace gateway latency stabilized during the September 8 backoff test.

cases.query: How do Rivet’s WAN-sync and local-debug compression policies differ, and why?

memories.text: Enable compression for Rivet WAN sync because its satellite link has limited bandwidth.
Disable compression for Rivet local debugging because plain payloads simplify inspection.
The Rivet WAN compression test cut transmitted bytes by 60 percent.
Rivet local-debug traces retained readable uncompressed payloads.
Rivet compression policy differs by WAN-sync and local-debug context.
An obsolete Rivet draft proposed compression for every environment.
Rivet local debugging listens on a Unix-domain socket.
Rivet’s WAN status icon is teal.
Raven enables compression for both local debugging and WAN sync.

cases.evidence_notes: Opposite verbs apply to different environments; neither policy supersedes the other.
